Subject: BRL invoicing - routing & intermediary fees question

Hi Karthik,

Quick question as we prepare the first monthly invoice: our treasury team is asking for a clear recommendation from Redwood on the best collection path for BRL. We currently receive payments in one of two ways:

1) USD wire into our US nostro (we then convert locally)
2) Local BRL payout via a partner/local bank (preferred by some customers)

The sticking point is intermediary/correspondent bank fees — our accounting needs direction on whether Redwood can provide an instruction that results in beneficiary-net (we receive the invoice amount net of any intermediary charges) or whether the sender (our customer) must cover all correspondent fees.

Can you confirm what Redwood typically recommends for Brazilian customers, and if you can provide a wire instruction template that minimizes ambiguous intermediary deductions? Also, if there are implications for VAT or GST reporting when we net fees, flag that for us.

Hi Carlos — thanks for the clear summary and the invoice. Short answer up front: we can support both rails, but the recommended path depends on the customer's tolerance for reconciliation complexity versus unit cost.

Options we typically present:
- Local BRL payout via local partner: lowest reconciliation friction for you, but it may incur a small local payout fee and requires an entity mapping on our side. Intermediary fees are typically absorbed by the routing bank unless you request sender-cover.
- USD nostro (sender wires USD): cleaner onboarding for Redwood (we settle into our USD account and convert), but correspondent deductions are more likely and can be ambiguous for the beneficiary.

For minimizing ambiguous deductions we normally provide a wire template that:
1) Includes our nostro account + full beneficiary details (tax id, remittance reference).
2) Adds an explicit instruction line: "Sender to pay all intermediary/correspondent charges; beneficiary to receive gross amount" OR "Beneficiary to accept net of intermediary charges" depending on what you want.

If Venda wants predictable landed amounts (no surprise nettings), ask customers to use sender-cover or use the local BRL payout. If you are OK with a small occasional mismatch and want the simpler UX, USD nostro is fine.

On VAT: Brazil VAT/GST doesn't change because of where the funds flow — it's more about who bears the cost (net vs gross) for accounting and whether you need to show a separate line for bank charges on invoices. If you net intermediary fees on your ledger, make sure the invoice/credit notes reflect that deduction so VAT reporting aligns.

I'm looping in our payments ops and finance folks to confirm wording and a wire template. I'll send a draft wire instruction that you can share with your customers.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer

Redwood Inference

Karthik — quick answers from ops / finance:

1) Customer-facing language (recommended):
   - If you want guaranteed landed amount: "Please select "OUR/SHOULD BE" (sender pays all intermediary/correspondent charges)"
   - If you want beneficiary to accept net deductions: "Please select "BEN/RECEIVER PAYS/NET" (beneficiary accepts intermediary/correspondent charges and will receive the invoice amount net of any deductions)."

   Keep it short — most corporate banks support a sender-cover flag in the payments UI.

2) Wire template: see attached draft (wire_template_BRL.docx) — includes full nostro details, Swift/IBAN where applicable, tax id for the beneficiary and a required invoice reference. We also added a line for "Sender to pay all intermediary/correspondent bank charges" as the default suggested text.

3) Entity mapping / lead time for local BRL payout: approx 7-10 business days once we receive beneficiary KYC + signed ACH/Wire authorization. Local payout will reduce the chance of ambiguous correspondent deductions but may incur a small payout fee (we list it on the invoice breakdown).

Note on VAT: our finance team prefers that if you take deductions on receipts, you issue a credit note that shows the bank fees separately so your VAT reporting remains auditable. If you want, we can add suggested language for the credit note template as well.

If that aligns, Karthik please reply to Venda with the wire template attached and set sender-cover as the primary recommendation for customers that require predictable landed amounts.
